mission: Torin weaponizes the Knights' suffering as argument — uses their pain to press his case for immediate, decisive action (i.e., his unilateral sacrifice). Sera watches and sees the Gavran pattern completing.
why_now: The human cost provides emotional ammunition for Torin's argument. The group is watching real people suffer.
conflict: Torin argues that these Knights are proof the seal cannot be maintained incrementally — it needs a permanent solution, now, and he's the only one qualified to provide it. His compassion is genuine. His conclusion is wrong.
turning_point: Sera's moment of truth: watching the outpost Knights suffer from lattice distortion, she recognizes that principled certainty alone — being right about the lattice — doesn't protect anyone. Ben's response to helplessness (leading without controlling) shows her a kind of leadership Gavran never demonstrated.
opening_hook: Torin kneels beside the young Knight who can't meditate. His hand on the Knight's shoulder is tender, genuine. His eyes, over the Knight's head, are cold with decision.
closing_hook: Sera doesn't argue with Torin this time. She turns to Ben instead. 'What is your plan, Skywalker?' Not conditional trust — a genuine question. She's stopped following Torin's framework. She's asking Ben to provide an alternative.
emotional_trajectory: Torin's compassion-as-argument -> Sera's recognition -> the shift from Torin to Ben

stakes.personal: Sera's arc moment of truth — she sees that rigidity isn't protection
stakes.interpersonal: The leadership dynamic shifting — Sera breaking from Torin's orbit
stakes.external: The Knights' suffering is real and demands response

setting: Jedi outpost — common area, the suffering Knights visible
sensory_details: Torin's hand on the Knight's shoulder — warm, steady, a commander's touch; his eyes cold over the gesture; Sera's jaw working as she processes; Ben's helplessness — he can't fix these Knights any more than he could fix the breach zone
action_beats: Torin kneels beside the young Knight and steadies her with a hand on her shoulder — tender, genuine, calculated
Sera's jaw works as she watches Torin weaponize the Knight's suffering into his argument
Sera turns away from Torin and faces Ben directly — her posture shifting from bystander to questioner
promises_paid: Sera's rigidity will break into principled flexibility (PP20 partial)
notes: Sera's arc: moment_of_truth. Her rigid principle (being right) fails to protect these Knights. Ben's response (honest helplessness rather than false authority) shows her something Gavran never did — a leader who admits he doesn't have the answer but won't stop looking.
